Proposals

Proposal planning, from the idea to the yes

A proposal is the only event where one of the two guests is not allowed to know it is happening, and that constraint changes everything. Tell us the rough date and area and we will pass your enquiry to planners who do this work.

Plan my proposalEngagement parties
  • Styled set-ups, photography and timing
  • Usually planned in four to eight weeks
  • Free to enquire

What does a proposal planner actually organise?

A proposal planner organises the place, the look, the timing and the photography, then protects the secret around all four. That means securing the location and any permission it needs, installing the set-up, briefing a photographer to be in position before you arrive, and packing down afterwards.

The reason people hire a marriage proposal planner is not the styling. It is that you cannot set up a surprise and be surprised by it at once. Someone has to be on site an hour early with the lanterns, and it cannot be you. Proposal planning services are usually sold as one fixed package for that reason.

The set-up

What is in a proposal setup?

A proposal setup is built from the same six pieces almost everywhere. What changes is the scale, and whether the location allows them.

No. 01

The location and its permission

Chosen first, because everything depends on what you may do there. Beaches and parks often need a permit.

No. 02

Styling and florals

An arch, a rug, a table, lanterns or a styled picnic. Outdoors it all has to survive wind and come away in minutes.

No. 03

Lighting

Candles, festoon or battery lanterns, depending on power. Lighting is what makes a dusk proposal photograph well.

No. 04

Signage and personal detail

A letter sign, a message or one object that means something only to you two. This is what people notice in the photos.

No. 05

Music

A speaker with a chosen song, or a musician out of sight. Check the site allows amplified sound first.

No. 06

A photographer, hidden nearby

Positioned early, briefed on where you will stand, shooting long from somewhere nobody looks.

The secret

How do you keep a proposal secret?

The set-up is the easy half. The cover story is the half that fails.

Every proposal has two plans running at once: the real one and the one the other person believes. A surprise proposal planner manages both, and the second is where the work is. The cover story has to explain why you are going somewhere specific, at a specific hour, dressed better than usual.

The stories that hold are the ones already normal for you: a dinner you would plausibly book, a walk you have done before. Elaborate ones fail, because they require the other person not to ask a follow up question.

Three rules. Keep the circle who know as small as possible. Put nothing in a shared calendar, bank account or photo library. And give them a reason to dress up that has nothing to do with you, because the most common tell is you insisting they change.

Tell the planner it is a surprise first

Say it in your opening message. It changes how a planner contacts you, which number they ring and what a quote email is titled.

Decide who is allowed to know

Write the list down. The leak almost always comes from someone who assumed the other person had already been told.

Timing

How long does it take to plan a proposal?

Most proposals in Australia come together in four to eight weeks. Under two weeks narrows your location and photographer options sharply.

01

Six to eight weeks out

Decide the date, the location type and the budget. If the site needs a permit, start it now, because some take weeks.

02

Four weeks out

Confirm the planner and photographer, settle the design and lock the exact time. Outdoors, sunset sets the time, not convenience.

03

Two weeks out

Build the cover story and test it out loud on someone. Confirm anyone helping. Check the ring is finished, sized and in your possession.

04

The week of

Watch the forecast, confirm the wet weather alternative in writing, and walk the site at the same hour.

Where

Where can you propose in Australia, and what needs permission?

Public does not mean available. This is the most common late discovery in proposal planning.

Common Australian proposal locations and the permission attached to each. Rules vary by council and park, so confirm yours in writing.
Location typeWhat it gives youPermission to checkWatch out for
Private property, a home or a rooftopTotal control, no permit and a roofThe owner, or the strata or building manager in an apartmentCrew access, lift bookings, and whether candles are allowed
A restaurant, bar or hotelWarmth, staff and a natural cover storyThe venue. Most allow a small set-up in a private area if you ask earlyOther diners, table timing, and holding the room
A beach, headland or lookoutThe best light in the countryThe council. Many require a permit; some cap numbers or ban structuresWind, which ruins candles and florals, plus everyone else there
A national park or council reserveScale, privacy and scenery you cannot buildThe park authority. A permit is common, takes weeks and has a feeWalk in distance, gate closing times, fire bans and no vehicles
A garden, botanic garden or wineryA styled backdrop with parking and toiletsThe gardens or venue management, which usually have a booking processOpening hours, other bookings, and rules about confetti
A helicopter, boat or hot air balloonA story that is impossible to topThe operator, who controls the schedule and the weather callCancellations, noise, and no room for a photographer

Photography

How does the planner brief the photographer?

Proposal photography is a short fixed booking, usually thirty to sixty minutes. The photographer arrives before you do, finds a clear sight line and a long lens, and stays out of view until the answer is yes, then shoots a short set of portraits. What they need from you is the direction you will approach from, the spot you will stop at, and a text as you leave the car.

Tell the photographer about the ring

A ring shot needs a clean background and ninety seconds of cooperation. Say early whether you want one, because it is easier to plan than to improvise.

Ask about the preview

You will want something to send your families that night. Ask how fast a preview set comes back, and whether video is included.

What goes wrong

The four things that actually go wrong

Ask any working proposal planner and the same four turn up.

The weather

Outdoor proposals in Australia lose more days to wind than rain. Wind takes out candles, florals and anything freestanding. Book the alternative when you book the first choice.

The cover story

The most common failure is not a leak. It is a story that does not survive a simple question, such as why you booked a table an hour from home on a Tuesday.

The ring

Resizing, delayed delivery and the wrong jacket cause more panic than anything else. Have it in your possession a week before.

Somebody talks

Usually by accident, from someone who assumed the news was already shared. If it leaks, propose anyway and do not tell them you know.

Ideas

Proposal ideas, sorted by the person you are proposing to

Good proposal ideas come from knowing the person, not from a list of trends.

If they hate being watched

A quiet beach at dawn, a lookout on a weekday morning, or your living room. Keep the styling small and the photographer far away.

If they love an audience

A restaurant full of people who know you, or a proposal followed by a party they did not know was booked. The trick is the handover: the moment happens privately, then a door opens.

If they are happiest outdoors

A sunrise walk, a headland at golden hour or a beach picnic. Check the permit early and keep the set-up light enough to carry.

If home is where they are happiest

Their favourite room, the back deck, or the first flat you shared. At home you control the weather, the light and the music, and can install it all while they are out.

If they are sentimental

Go back somewhere with history: the bar where you met, the beach from your first trip. Build the styling from your own material, such as photographs or a letter.

If they travel for everything

Propose at the start of a trip rather than the end, so the rest of the holiday becomes the celebration. Overseas, book a local photographer rather than hiding a friend.

Next

After the yes

An engagement party usually follows three to four months later, and the guest list you build for it has consequences for the wedding.

Straight answers

Proposal planning questions

What does a proposal planner cost in Australia?

There is no reliable published national benchmark, so treat any single figure with caution. What moves the price is the location and whether it needs a paid permit, the size of the proposal setup, whether photography is included, and how far the crew has to carry it. A picnic on a beach and a rooftop build with live music are not the same product.

How far in advance should I book a proposal planner?

Four to eight weeks is the usual window for proposal planning services. Start earlier for a national park or council reserve, because permits take weeks and are the most common cause of a changed plan.

Do I need a permit to propose on a beach or in a park?

Often yes, once you are installing anything. Many councils and park authorities require a booking or permit for a set-up on public land, may charge a fee, and may restrict structures, candles and vehicles. A marriage proposal planner who works in that area will know the process and can lodge it.

Will a photographer really stay hidden?

Yes, and it is a normal part of the job. They arrive early, work from distance with a long lens, and blend into a place where people take photographs anyway.

Can a planner organise a proposal without the other person finding out?

That is the core of the brief. Say it is a surprise in your first message and a surprise proposal planner will adjust how they contact you and what emails are titled.

One enquiry, then it is somebody else's job

The rough date, the area, the kind of place you have in mind and whether anyone else knows.
